__note_chunked_export_maps: The two rule pairs below exist because the CHUNKED bundle format (2.1.242+) moved where the original names live. On a monolithic build, `utils/auth.js` etc. each carry a big `RealName: () => minifiedId` map, which is why FOUR export_map rules produce 673 of that tree's 725 renames. In a chunked build those per-module maps are gone from the anchor modules — the anchors' own files export via a bare ESM `export { minified, ... }` list, which carries NO original names at all (measured: 1,189 names in entrypoints/sdk/coreSchemas.js, none recoverable). Name-carrying maps DO still exist, but in DIFFERENT files. Measured strict `key: () => bareIdentifier` pairs sitting in a file that also has a function-valued entry (the only shape findExportMapObject can anchor on): 3,074 on 2.1.238, 1,966 on 2.1.259, 312 on 2.1.260. So the recovery route on chunked trees is to anchor the files that still hold such a map. Each rule below was authored against a PRE-RENAME tree (STOP_AFTER_STEP=2.5) and verified on BOTH 2.1.259 and 2.1.260.
__note_export_map_collision_hazard: An export_map walk binds the FIRST object literal containing `<key>: () => <anchorName>`, matching on the anchor's MINIFIED name. In files where the minifier reuses a short name heavily this is a real mis-binding hazard, not a theoretical one: in components/PromptInput/useSwarmBanner.js the anchor `userFacingName` minifies to `ne`, and `ne` occurs as an arrow body ~10 times in that file for entirely unrelated values. That candidate was DROPPED rather than shipped — it happened to fail closed, but it could as easily have bound the wrong map. Before adding a rule here, check that the anchor's minified target is used as a map value exactly ONCE (`=> <name>` followed by , } or whitespace).
